I'm new to this sub, but since I love enchiladas and make them on occasion, I will share a technique that helps tremendously in the preparation process. First off, make your enchiladas with corn tortillas (red ones if you can find them) instead of the flour tortillas. Corn tortillas tend to crack and break when rolled, especially if they are cold. I was taught to (very) lightly fry the tortilla prior to filling and rolling them. I use a shallow fry pan just a little larger than the tortilla with about 1/4 inch of cooking oil in it (corn oil works best for flavor). Heat the oil just hot enough for a tortilla to lightly bubble and sizzle when dipped into it. When you have the oil just right, put one corn tortilla into the oil for about 3 to 5 seconds. Flip it and do another 3 to 5 seconds on the other side if the oil did not cover both sides when cooking the first side. Remove the tortilla carefully so it doesn't tear and pat the excess oil off with a paper towel stack. Now the tortilla is soft enough to fill and roll without breaking or tearing. It's easy to get a good rhythm down once you get the hang of it- fry, dry, fill, roll and place in a pan. This will let you make a whole lot of delicious enchiladas quickly so you can get to the eating much faster.
Enchilada Pro Tip: lightly fry your corn tortillas before rolling them
